label: Suspected Asbestos / Fibro Sheeting or Lagging
volunteer_identification_guide: Fibrous cement wall/roof sheets (Hardies Fibrolite / Wunderlich Durabestos) or pipe insulation lagging; severe inhalation hazard if weathered, cracked, or broken; DO NOT DISTURB.

label: Flaking Lead-Based Paint
volunteer_identification_guide: Chalking or peeling paint on old timber or ironwork; contains toxic white lead pigment; ingestible/inhalable dust hazard; wash hands.

label: Unstable Roof / Walls / Rotten Floorboards
volunteer_identification_guide: Termite-eaten bearers, rotten flooring, sagging ceiling rafters, or bowing unbraced masonry walls prone to sudden structural collapse.

label: Sub-floor Chemical / Arsenic / Pesticide Hazard
volunteer_identification_guide: Arsenic-based sheep dip residue, rat baits under floors, or organochlorine pesticides (aldrin/dieldrin); wear nitrile gloves, avoid skin contact with subfloor soils.

label: Snakes / Spiders / Wasps / Guano / Hantavirus
volunteer_identification_guide: Redback spiders under sills/troughs, brown snakes in foundations, wasps in roof cavities, and histoplasmosis/fungal spores in accumulated bat/pigeon guano; wear P2 mask and boots.

label: Safe for Full Internal Entry
volunteer_identification_guide: Building structurally sound, floors secure, no active chemical or biological hazard preventing entry.

label: Partial Entry Only (Restricted Zones)
volunteer_identification_guide: Entry permitted into specific sound rooms only; unstable wings or rotten floor zones strictly barricaded or excluded.

label: Exterior Recording Only (Unsafe to Enter)
volunteer_identification_guide: Roof collapse imminent, dense asbestos debris, or total lack of sound flooring; all observations recorded from external perimeter.

label: Good / Intact (>70% Original Fabric)
volunteer_identification_guide: Building structurally sound and weathertight; high degree of original integrity across framing, cladding, and joinery.

label: Fair / Modified (30-70% Original Fabric)
volunteer_identification_guide: Substantially standing but exhibits roof leaks, timber decay, altered internal spaces, or loss of secondary features.

label: Poor / Ruinous (<30% Original Fabric)
volunteer_identification_guide: Partially or completely collapsed; roof gone, framing decayed, walls freestanding or fallen into archaeological rubble mound.

label: Vertical Seam / Crack in Wall Junction
volunteer_identification_guide: Unbonded vertical joint or straight crack where an extension was built abutting an existing wall without tying masonry or timber plates.

label: Change in Brick, Stone or Timber Conversion
volunteer_identification_guide: Clear demarcation in material (e.g., pit-sawn to circular-sawn, handmade brick to pressed brick, beaded weatherboard to plain).

label: Roof Framing / Batten Discontinuity in Attic
volunteer_identification_guide: Break in rafter spacing, new roof timbers butted against older rafters, or batten line changes in roof cavity confirming phased enlargement.

label: Lead Flashing Line / Crease on Exterior Wall
volunteer_identification_guide: Stepped groove or copper/lead flashing remnant on wall indicating where a former verandah, skillion, or covered way once abutted.

label: Blocked Door / Window Opening
volunteer_identification_guide: Infilled masonry aperture, different boarding across former frame, or interior plaster scar indicating an altered circulation route.

label: Step in Floor Level or Board Width Shift
volunteer_identification_guide: Change in finished floor elevation (100-200mm drop into lean-to) or sudden transition from 150mm butt boards to 100mm T&G boards.

label: Ceiling / Wall Joist Scar from Removed Partition
volunteer_identification_guide: Unpainted line, patched plaster band, or empty mortises in ceiling joists revealing where an internal dividing wall once stood.

label: Stage 1: Original Core Structure
volunteer_identification_guide: The earliest identifiable phase of the building envelope, primary structural framing, and initial footings.

label: Stage 2: Early Addition / Extension
volunteer_identification_guide: First major expansion (e.g., rear skillion range, covered way to detached kitchen, wing extension, or added verandah).

label: Stage 3: Later Modification / Infill
volunteer_identification_guide: Secondary modifications (e.g., enclosing verandahs for sleepouts, re-roofing shingles in corrugated iron, installing cast-iron stove).

label: Stage 4: Modern Repairs / Salvage / Abandonment
volunteer_identification_guide: Late 20th-century interventions (steel posts, concrete patches, corrugated zincalume repairs, machinery removal, or roof collapse).
